newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields continue to grind up at bearish close.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields continue to grind up at bearish close.

text.p: New Zealand debt continued to grind higher at Tuesday's close as bearish sentiment closed in on the market.
Bond yields, which have been hyper-sensitive to offshore developments of late, went beyond the call of duty in tracking U.S. Treasuries and underperformed the dollar bloc during the session.

Dealers said that following the heavy selling seen on Friday, bonds had staged a tentative recovery on Monday because the U.S. and Australian markets rallied. That soon fell to pieces as offshore fortunes turned once more, and the market's tone grew increasingly softer on Tuesday.
"Everyone is questioning: why should New Zealand outperform at this point in time given the data of yesterday, the retail sales and house prices, wasn't the best?" one dealer said.
Retail sales grew a surprisingly strong 3.4 percent in January, while the national median house price rose 4.2 percent in the February year.

The mid-bonds ended Tuesday's session nine basis points higher in yield at 7.73 percent, while the 10-year maturity was up six at 7.86 percent. Dealers said volumes were fairly light, especially in the longer bonds.
"Those who wanted to buy, I think, bought yesterday, and there hasn't really been too much follow-through today," a dealer said.
He said the Reserve Bank's easing of monetary conditions last week had surprised the market.

"It should have been a positive surprise but sentiment got swamped straight away by what happened in the offshore markets, so I think that really hurt those out there who were bullish, because the market just can't gain any ground at all."
In the money market, 90-day bank bills finished five basis points weaker at 7.52 percent as the currency's Trade-Weighted Index slipped to 68.34 from 68.39 at Monday's close.
The overnight cash rate climbed to 7.45 percent from 7.30 percent at Monday's close.
